The May guide requires permission and a record of written opt-in, with payment authorization, frequency and timing, amount determination, and a cancellation policy when setting up a subscription. The same May guide shows a customer-configured Accounts v2 Account via customer_account or Customers v1 Customer via customer. Accounts v2 is dated GA for Connect users and public preview with a preview version for other participants. The preview-access sentence is incomplete. Both customer variants are shown for creation, Checkout setup, SetupIntent creation, save-during-payment PaymentIntent, and saved-method charging, without pairs for every call (old raw lines 29-86, 105-135, 155-219, 221-257, 449-518 and 522-570).

May hosted Checkout uses a server-created Checkout Session in setup mode, with both card and kr_card in both examples and redirect to the returned session URL. Its setup test UI authorizes or fails payment setup, with no completed charge described (old raw lines 88-139). Direct no-charge setup creates a server SetupIntent, with usage on_session or off_session in prose and off_session in examples, and exposes the SetupIntent's client secret to browser Stripe.js for confirmKrCardSetup, return_url and online mandate data inferred from that client. The named Dahlia train is May example evidence (old raw lines 201-380).

May Direct API saving during a payment creates a separate PaymentIntent, sets setup_future_usage=off_session and confirm=true, and uses mandate_data if a mandate must be created. The shown server mandate data includes IP and user agent. Later charging creates and confirms a new KRW PaymentIntent with the saved PaymentMethod ID and matching customer identity. Set off_session to true when the customer is outside the checkout flow for that PaymentIntent. Recurring capture uses automatic. Server detach deactivates the reusable method and sends mandate.updated and payment_method.detached (old raw lines 442-570).

The May standalone manual PaymentIntent redirect checks requires_action and redirect_to_url together and returns PaymentIntent identifiers for status verification, with a webhook recommended. The later Direct API testing paragraph calls the UI Checkout but describes PaymentIntent status transitions from requires_action to succeeded or requires_payment_method. Keep those sandbox PaymentIntent states separate from the hosted Checkout setup test at line 139 (old raw lines 382-440 and 572-574).

contributions.original_prompts:
New raw: `raw/stripe-payments-kr-card-set-up-future-payments-2026-11-07.md`. Prior raw: `raw/stripe-kr-card-set-up-future-payments-2025.md`. Current summaries: `wiki/sources/source-stripe-kr-card-set-up-future-payments.md`.

- Q1: For `https://docs.stripe.com/payments/kr-card/set-up-future-payments`, what central documented behavior, prerequisites, identities and state boundaries does the complete new capture establish, and how does it compare with the matched old capture and every mapped current summary?

- Q2: Which changes are substantive versus presentational or navigation-only? Which historical claims must remain dated, which conflicts need reciprocal warnings, and which API, UI, version, client/server or outcome qualifications prevent unsupported inferences?

reviewed_answers.Q1: The November 7 capture at https://docs.stripe.com/payments/kr-card/set-up-future-payments states that a merchant can save local South Korean cards for later charges and points to Checkout and Direct API variants (new raw lines 5-14). The mapped source-stripe-kr-card-set-up-future-payments.md summarizes the May 8 mechanics. May requires permission and a written agreement record and attaches the method to a customer-configured Account through customer_account or to a Customer through customer. It describes Accounts v2 as generally available for Connect and in public preview with preview versioning for other users. Hosted Checkout creates a setup-mode session with card and kr_card in the May examples and redirects to the returned hosted URL. Direct API no-charge setup creates a SetupIntent server-side and uses its client secret with browser confirmKrCardSetup and mandate data. A distinct PaymentIntent can save during a payment using setup_future_usage=off_session and conditional mandate data. The later PaymentIntent uses the saved PaymentMethod and the corresponding customer identity, sets off_session=true when the customer is absent from checkout, and uses automatic capture for recurring payments. Server-side detachment deactivates the method and emits mandate.updated and payment_method.detached. The mapped summary conveys the main flow and the ngn anomaly but omits the preview version and the requires_action guard and status verification for the separate manual redirect PaymentIntent. Setup and browser return are separate from charging and payment-status verification (old raw lines 29-139, old raw lines 155-380, old raw lines 382-440 and old raw lines 449-574).
reviewed_answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/kr-card/set-up-future-payments, the November change is navigation. The two variant URLs replace detailed Checkout and Direct API bodies while retaining the save-for-later purpose (new raw lines 5-14). Keep the May 8 behavior in source-stripe-kr-card-set-up-future-payments.md dated, including customer consent, the two distinct customer identifiers and preview versioning, server intent creation, browser confirmation on the Dahlia example, redirect and status checks, and deactivation events (old raw lines 29-139, old raw lines 155-380 and old raw lines 382-574). Carry a reciprocal Korea concept warning for ngn in both May kr_card save-during-payment examples versus krw in the manual redirect and reuse examples, supported by separately dated Korean acceptance and subscription currency guidance (old raw lines 395-404, old raw lines 469-517 and old raw lines 535-565). The same concept should qualify its group-level manual capture property with automatic capture for recurring kr_card, distinguish the optional manual PaymentIntent redirect from saving, and keep the SetupIntent client secret distinct from PaymentIntent client secrets despite the parenthetical at old raw lines 259-261. The dated PaymentIntent test transitions from requires_action to succeeded or requires_payment_method. The separate hosted Checkout test authorizes or fails payment setup (old raw lines 137-139 and old raw lines 572-574). Current variant parameters, account eligibility, end-to-end setup, payment success and settlement remain unverified.
